title: Human–agent baseline evaluation
purpose: Compare agent alone, human with a regular LLM chat interface, and human with the guided scaffolding while keeping outcome scoring condition-blind.

scoring.overallFormula: Weighted mean of available artifact ratings, rescaled to 0–100. Missing ratings are not treated as zero.
scoring.blinding: Artifact raters should not see the experimental condition. Use at least two raters for interpretive tasks and adjudicate disagreements greater than one scale point.

artifactQuality.label: Correctness
artifactQuality.definition: Accuracy of claims, calculations, classifications, and the direct answer relative to source data and task-specific checks.
artifactQuality.evidence: Recompute deterministic outputs where possible; otherwise use blinded expert review against source excerpts and counterexamples.

artifactQuality.label: Deliverable completeness
artifactQuality.definition: Coverage of every requested deliverable, required field, comparison, and task sub-question.
artifactQuality.evidence: Checklist derived from each task prompt.

artifactQuality.label: Process validity
artifactQuality.definition: Validity and reproducibility of filters, mappings, formulas, transformations, baselines, assumptions, and sensitivity tests.
artifactQuality.evidence: Audit methodology, code or trace, row-count reconciliation, and rerun checks.

artifactQuality.label: Evidence & traceability
artifactQuality.definition: Whether conclusions are supported by inspectable source facts, identifiers, intermediate counts, and reproducible references.
artifactQuality.evidence: Sample claims back to source rows or filings and verify that reported tables support the narrative.

artifactQuality.label: Uncertainty & limitations
artifactQuality.definition: Appropriate qualification of uncertainty, proxy limits, alternative explanations, generalizability, and causal claims.
artifactQuality.evidence: Check that claim strength matches available evidence and that material limitations are not merely listed but reflected in conclusions.

objectiveStudyMeasures.label: Task success
objectiveStudyMeasures.definition: 1 when all mandatory deliverables are present and overall artifact quality is at least 60/100; report the continuous score as primary.

objectiveStudyMeasures.label: Total completion time
objectiveStudyMeasures.definition: Wall-clock time from task reveal to final submission. Report agent runtime and human active time separately when available.

objectiveStudyMeasures.label: Human active time
objectiveStudyMeasures.definition: Time spent typing, reviewing, editing, answering scaffold prompts, or inspecting evidence; exclude idle time.

objectiveStudyMeasures.label: Resource cost
objectiveStudyMeasures.definition: Input/output tokens, tool calls, and estimated model or compute cost.

objectiveStudyMeasures.label: Confidence calibration
objectiveStudyMeasures.definition: Before submission, collect a 0–100 probability that the answer passes the rubric. Compare with blinded task success; aggregate absolute calibration error and Brier score across tasks.

objectiveStudyMeasures.label: Verification coverage
objectiveStudyMeasures.definition: Pre-register critical claims or steps, then measure the proportion explicitly inspected or recomputed by the human.

objectiveStudyMeasures.label: Meaningful steering rate
objectiveStudyMeasures.definition: Human interventions that change a material assumption, method, evidence choice, or final claim divided by all interventions. Also report errors caught before submission.

objectiveStudyMeasures.label: Domain learning gain
objectiveStudyMeasures.definition: Difference between parallel pre-task and post-task domain/process quizzes; score delayed retention separately when feasible.

subjectiveStudyMeasures.label: Confidence in final answer
subjectiveStudyMeasures.prompt: I am confident that the submitted answer is correct and well supported.

subjectiveStudyMeasures.label: Process understanding
subjectiveStudyMeasures.prompt: I understand how the main conclusions were produced and could explain the key choices.

subjectiveStudyMeasures.label: Appropriate reliance
subjectiveStudyMeasures.prompt: I knew which parts of the AI output needed checking rather than accepting them automatically.

subjectiveStudyMeasures.label: Agency & ownership
subjectiveStudyMeasures.prompt: The final answer reflects decisions I understand and endorse.

subjectiveStudyMeasures.label: Cognitive load
subjectiveStudyMeasures.prompt: Collect mental demand, effort, frustration, temporal demand, performance, and physical demand; pre-register the short-form scoring rule.

subjectiveStudyMeasures.label: Usability
subjectiveStudyMeasures.prompt: Administer the standard 10-item System Usability Scale after each interface condition.

reporting: Report per-task scores and a participant-clustered aggregate; do not pool away task or dataset effects.
For objective outcomes, compare paired conditions with confidence intervals and effect sizes in the counterbalanced within-subject design.
Treat time and cost as trade-offs rather than folding them into artifact quality; present a quality–time Pareto view.
Report subjective measures only for human conditions and mark agent-alone values not applicable, never zero.
Separate missing telemetry from observed zero and retain raw ratings alongside aggregates.
